title: Interview candidate: David (@yonderdavid.bsky.social), who posted synth choirs, a singing cat and polyhedra instruments and answered questions about each
summary: David (971 followers) posted four sets of videos in the window and answered what people asked under each. 13 Nov: a choir of Chimera vocal synth heads singing the Kyrie from Palestrina's Missa Papae Marcelli, reposted twice the same day with changes other members suggested. 13 to 16 Nov: after a member remarked that the synth's animal voices had no cat, a quartet plus a simulated cat voice singing "Poor Wayfaring Stranger", then "Factory Girl" on request. 17 Nov: instruments made of polyhedra playing "Sakura Sakura" in a landscape of polyhedra, followed by a post-by-post account of how he made it. The card lists 14 of his replies with the post each one answered.

candidate.source: Found by the researcher in posts.jsonl; he is not in the digest's Interview material. The digest lists the five members with the most question-and-answer pairs. By my own count with a similar rule he has 14 such pairs from 6 askers, around twentieth among members.

checks.optOutList: not on the opt-out list (packages/scraper/config/optout.json, loaded through the tool)
checks.bio: not checked: the digest carries no bios and research has no network. The scraper reports that it excluded accounts with profile opt-outs before the digest was written.
checks.windowPosts: Read all 58 of his posts in the window. Three are top-level, all videos; the rest are replies, almost all in threads about things he made. Nothing out of bounds found, and none of his posts carries a sensitivity mark in the data. No post asks not to be quoted.

didInWindow: Posted videos made with the open-source Chimera vocal synth (another developer's project, github.com/jamesondh/chimera-vocal-synth) and with instrument sounds he says come from physical simulation: a synth head playing a falling-block game by voice command (13 Nov, 78 likes), a six-part choir (13 Nov, 124 likes, then two revised versions), a quartet with a simulated cat voice, guitar and fiddle (14 Nov, 65 likes), a two-voice "Factory Girl" with fiddles and cello (16 Nov), and polyhedra instruments playing "Sakura Sakura" (17 Nov, 61 likes). He said the polyhedra video was rendered in Blender through its Python API, driven by Claude from his descriptions, and he posted the stills from each revision.
couldBeShown: The choir video and its two revisions (13 Nov). Alt text: "A choir of Chimera vocal synths sing the Kyrie 1 from Palestrina's Missa Papae Marcelli in six-part harmony."

The cat quartet video (14 Nov). Alt text: "A quartet of chimera-vocal-synth voices, plus a physically simulated feline voice, sing \"Poor Wayfaring Stranger,\" accompanied by physically simulated guitar and fiddle."
The animal-voice sample video (13 Nov). Alt text: "A chimera-vocal-synth critter demo."

The polyhedra video (17 Nov). Alt text: "Animated instruments composed of polyhedra play the Japanese folk tune さくら さくら while the camera explores a landscape composed of regular polyhedra. The landscape features many sakura trees."
The koto simulation code he shared on request (pastebin.com/cxLPkJby), and the revision stills in his walkthrough posts.
The researcher has read the alt texts only and has not watched or heard the videos.

posts.text: this works incredibly well, was there an unseen graveyard of failures or what's your theory of what went on here

The plan was a quartet of male voices (the female synth voices need repair; see the soprano line in the Kyrie). I think the harmony helped fill out the voice a bit and the instruments sounding almost lifelike (the bowing should reverse on long notes) helped make the overall vibe ungoofy.

The articulation needed a couple repairs: nonzero airflow on the J and an exaggerated release on the D. I called the other sounds good enough. The meow and yowl took some work and iteration against reference recordings. The original yowl sounded like a kazoo.

sensitive: Under 1,000 followers and not someone who usually gets attention, so he should appear only as the hero of the moment (R7). He is one of the scraper's seed accounts, and the scope review warns that seeds lead the top of the story list (he leads stories 2 and 3), so other lanes will probably carry the same videos. Ten of the 14 prompts come from two accounts that were in the previous episode (@norvid-studies.bsky.social spoke, @shimmermathlabs.com was shown). The asker in the "voices" pair is the show's owner; the show is not its own subject, so that pair may be better left alone. The "piano" pair is about his offline life (R1): he said it in public in this thread, but I would leave it out unless a reviewer disagrees. The two "covers" pairs are about copyright in general, not about anyone's legal trouble. The Chimera vocal synth is another person's project, and he names its maker as active on another site; anything shown should credit both. Nothing listed is an argument or a complaint.
